title: Two worlds, one list of gaps

data.source: Five toy rotor worlds, 33,000 gaps each (300 replicas, seed 11), generated in the script. Adapted from colloquy/lab/metaphysical/rival_readings.py with the same seeds.

prediction: From the list of gaps alone an enduring world and an inheriting world cannot be told apart (the lens's P4 and P8); only forging the record or scrubbing the state at the cut separates them (P6).
baseline: The steady-state Kalman filter (Muth 1960): an exponential average is also the best steady predictor of a hidden lasting state. And world R, where nothing crosses, as the null.

numbers.E_after_forging_the_record: unchanged by construction (no record to forge)

why: A list of gaps told "nothing crosses" from "only the last occasion" from "more than the last occasion". It did not tell an inherited summary from a thing that endures: an enduring toy world, retuned after the lens's own blind attempt missed, copies the inheriting world within 0.0108 at lags one to four. Two interventions do separate them in the toy: forge the record, or scrub the state at the cut. Seven of the lens's eight predictions held; the mimic prediction failed as written.
variant: V-metaphysical-1 (the empty cut as a screening claim; world W's redraw rule): a museum experiment, not the owner's CRR
would_make_it_testable: An intervention, not more watching: forge the record the seed reads (the inheriting world changes, the enduring one does not), or scrub the fast state at the cut (the enduring world changes, the inheriting one does not).

forks.what: two tunings of the enduring mimic

second_check: re-run by a library worker who did not write the worlds; not checked by a person
variants: V-metaphysical-1 (the empty cut as a screening claim): a museum experiment, not the owner's CRR
operating_characteristics: With 33,000 gaps a correlation has a standard error near 0.006, so the tolerances are several standard errors wide. The answer rests on whether a mimic can be tuned, which is a search and not a chance event.
